claims.head: McKenna’s line gets the soft minutes
claims.call: The Maple Leafs’ L3 (McKenna, Paul and Joshua) spends at least 24% of its 5-on-5 time against the Wild’s fourth line, against about 14% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Maple Leafs keep sending McKenna’s line (McKenna, Paul and Joshua) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jim Hiller has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Wild’s fourth line is M. Foligno, Hartman and N. Foligno.

notes.text: Kirill Marchenko is on injured reserve and has missed the last 6 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Easton Cowan has taken his spot beside Jack Roslovic and Auston Matthews. That line has had 57% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 37:32 together, down from 72% with Marchenko.

Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson. That pair has had 61% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 47:25 together, up from 48% with Blankenburg.
Morgan Rielly is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Dakota Mermis has taken his spot beside Troy Stecher.
Ryan Tverberg was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside John Tavares and William Nylander.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Wild go in first in the Central with 30 points, the Maple Leafs seventh in the Atlantic with 18 points.

TOR.head: The Maple Leafs face a real test
TOR.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs can pull it off if their power play gets going.

MIN.head: The Wild have a lot going for them
MIN.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

story.head: The Maple Leafs are searching for answers
paras: The Maple Leafs are on a four-game losing streak, while the Wild (13-3-4) beat Montréal 2-1 in overtime on Tuesday. Going in, the Wild are first in the Central (tied for second in the NHL) and the Leafs seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 21st).
The Wild’s record (.750) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.649), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Maple Leafs’ record (.450) is about what their chances are worth.

The Wild let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd), leave the shooting to their forwards (3rd lowest) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.20 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd) and have had shaky goaltending (31st). The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Maple Leafs. On top of that, both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Kirill Kaprizov (17 G / 15 A / 32 P in 20 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is fourth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. Quinn Hughes (6 G / 21 A / 27 P in 20 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games. Auston Matthews (11 G / 17 A / 28 P in 20 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is sixth in the NHL, and William Nylander (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 20 GP) is next in line.
Jesper Wallstedt (12-2-3 / .924 SV% in 17 GS) has been a rock in net for Minnesota and is expected to start. Anthony Stolarz (5-2-0 / .907 SV% in 7 GS) is expected to go for Toronto.

At home, Jim Hiller likes to send McKenna, Paul and Joshua out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against M. Foligno, Hartman and N. Foligno. One more thing: the Wild usually control more of the chances than the Maple Leafs do.

items.text: The Wild have been without Filip Gustavsson all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start.
The Maple Leafs are newly without Morgan Rielly, and have been without Kirill Marchenko and Nick Blankenburg for several games.
Joel Eriksson Ek has five goals on chances worth about 10.3 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Kirill Kaprizov and Quinn Hughes have a point in nine straight games.
